subject: Runtime for multivariate GWAS with large number of traits and SNPs

messages.author: d2c2af4f1e7d97c6
messages.subject: Runtime for multivariate GWAS with large number of traits and SNPs
parts:
Hi,

I would appreciate for your help with the following issue I have,

I am interested in conducting multivariate GWAS with 11 clinical traits that are genetically correlated among each other. The individual GWAS summary statistics for these 11 traits contains ~30 million SNPs. Therefore, it seems like running userGWAS might take unrealistically long time.

Do you have any suggestions on how to proceed with such data?

My model specification is as follows,

model<-"F1 =~ trait 1 + trait 2 + trait 3 + trait 4 + trait 5

F2 =~ trait 6 + trait 7  + trait 8 + trait 9 + trait 10 + trait 11

F1~~F2

F1 ~ SNP

F2 ~ SNP"


best wishes,

Pashupati

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: Runtime for multivariate GWAS with large number of traits and SNPs
parts:
Hi Pashupati, 

There are two main things you can to do when you have that many SNPs: 
1. The estimated model for each SNP is independent of all other SNPs, so you can split the runs up as much as is possible (e.g., by submitting different batches of SNPs to different jobs on a computing cluster).

2. If you can, run in parallel using multiple cores (ideally within separate jobs). 

Best, 
  Andrew
